title: Synthetic-probe conductor for Canary rollback
creator: Asha Gupta
description: Introduce a synthetic-probe based conductor service that augments canary and A/B rollout gates with targeted synthetic inputs, hierarchical thresholds, and graded retraction policies. The goal is to detect regressions tied to config/model flips earlier and provide automated, explainable rollback actions with root-cause tags and a minimally disruptive hysteresis window.
background: Current deployment eval gates rely primarily on sampled production traffic and metric drift. We've seen two issues where sparse but high-severity failure modes (hallucination on long prompts, formatting regressions for structured outputs) escaped detection until user reports. Synthetic probes—short, curated input sets designed to stress known failure dimensions—can provide deterministic signals that complement sampled traffic and allow earlier intervention.
implementation_plan: Design probe taxonomy: groups for hallucination, factuality, structured-output format, latency-sensitive long-context, and auth-sensitive prompts.

Build conductor microservice that schedules probe runs against candidate variants (canary/A vs B), collects model responses, and computes multi-metric scorecards (pass/fail per probe + aggregated risk score).
Integrate conductor with rollout-controller: expose an /eval-result webhook that the controller uses to influence traffic split and trigger reversion actions.
Implement hierarchical gating logic: soft-warning -> pause traffic ramp -> partial rollback -> full rollback, with time-based hysteresis to avoid flapping.
Add provenance and root-cause tagging: include probe id, model config diff, top-k failure reasons, and candidate PR link in rollback event metadata.
Ship a UI panel in Console (canary tab) with probe histograms, signal timelines, and recommended rollback action with one-click execute for SRE/PMs.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor service runs scheduled probe suites against canary variants within 30s of candidate spin-up and completes within the defined probe timeout (default 90s).
Rollout-controller ingests eval results and automatically initiates policy-driven actions (pause/ramp-down/rollback) without manual intervention for high-confidence failures.
All rollback events created by the conductor include a root-cause tag and a generated GitHub PR/issue template link summarizing the failure for follow-up.
Console shows probe-level pass/fail rates and a timeline for the last 7 days for any model/config pair.
End-to-end tests (integration) demonstrate a synthetic-probe-triggered rollback in staging with telemetry and postmortem stub created automatically.
testing_plan: Unit tests for conductor scoring logic covering edge cases and numeric stability.
Integration test: deploy a canary with a deliberate formatting regression, assert synthetic probes detect and trigger partial rollback within configured thresholds.
Chaos test: simulate intermittent probe backend failures and ensure controller honors missing data (no false-positive rollback).
A/B experiment in staging: compare detection lead-time vs sampled-production-only eval for 50 rolling releases.
Manual QA: PM/Design-run through Console panel for clarity and one-click rollback path.
monitoring_playbook: alerts: probe-suite-failure-rate > 5% for 5m -> P1 ops page, probe-delta-risk > threshold -> notify-runbook-channel #release-safety
runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rollout-safety/synthetic-probes-playbook (includes rollback verification steps and stakeholder notifications)
incident artifact generation: automated postmortem stub and linking to rollback event and GitHub issue.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: synthetic probes generate false positives for benign model variation. Mitigation: multi-probe aggregation with weighted thresholds and require at least two independent probe groups to trigger high-confidence rollback.
Risk: probes increase test load and cost. Mitigation: adaptive scheduling (run full probe suite only at key milestones; lightweight probes every minute).
Risk: new attack vector if probes expose prompts. Mitigation: store probes in encrypted vault, restrict access, and sanitize probe outputs in logs.
notes: Related RFC draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abc-Probe-RFC (internal) - uses probe taxonomy introduced by Research/Applied ML.
Design request submitted to Design (DES-401) for Console panel mockups; PM feedback cycle scheduled for 2025-01-20.
SRE asked for a k8s resource budget: 2 vCPU, 4 GiB mem, burstable to 4 vCPU for probe concurrency.
